title: how do you make a multi-provider AI system measurable?
description: How to make a multi-provider AI system measurable by observing every model call at one chokepoint.
tldr: A multi-provider AI system becomes measurable when observability sits at the single model-call chokepoint. Record the model, usage, latency, and outcome there.

sections.h2: where should observability sit in a multi-provider AI system?
body: Put it at the single model-call chokepoint. Every provider call passes through that integration, giving the system one place to capture the same measurements.
One well-placed integration can make the whole system measurable without scattering observability across every provider-specific path.

sections.h2: what should you record at the model-call chokepoint?
body: Record the model, usage, latency, and outcome for each call. Those fields create a consistent view across the system's model providers.
The point is to capture the receipt where the call happens, while the model choice, resource usage, timing, and result are all available together.

sections.h2: why does one integration make the whole system measurable?
body: A shared model-call chokepoint gives every provider call the same observability boundary. The integration becomes the place where the system's model activity can be measured consistently.
The practical question is simple: where is your model-call chokepoint today? That location determines whether measurement is centralized or scattered.

faqs.q: How do you measure a multi-provider AI system?
faqs.a: Place observability at the single model-call chokepoint. Record the model, usage, latency, and outcome for each call.

faqs.q: What metrics should be recorded for every model call?
faqs.a: Record the model, usage, latency, and outcome. These are the measurements identified for the model-call chokepoint.

faqs.q: Why use a model-call chokepoint for observability?
faqs.a: A single integration can cover the whole multi-provider system when every model call passes through it. This creates one place to record consistent measurements.
